caption:
Accenture now pays for just $29 of Claude use per employee each month.
Anything more must be billed to a project or team, per an internal memo.
Some heavy users had been spending up to $1,000 a month.

Should companies put a budget on AI at work?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: 404 Media via GIGAZINE

slides.headline: Some Accenture staff spent $1,000 a month on Claude. Now they get *$29*

slides.heading: The *$29 rule*
paras: Accenture now centrally funds $29 per employee per month for Claude. The change took effect October 1, and all Claude Enterprise costs are now usage-based.
Anything above $29 must be charged to a specific project or team. An internal memo warned that licenses are reviewed and can be reallocated.

slides.heading: Heavy users *hit hard*
paras: Some employees had been spending $500 to $1,000 a month on Claude, according to 404 Media, which first reported the memo.
Some are now trying to move to Premium accounts, which include $250 in token usage a week. One said the upgrade looked blocked.

slides.heading: The end of *unlimited AI*
paras: Accenture says it still makes AI available to all its people and wants the right tool for the right work.
It is not alone. Uber capped staff at $1,500 a month per AI tool, and Microsoft gave each division a token budget.

paras.t: AI at work now comes with a budget.

slides.hook: Your company's AI budget could be next. Follow to see who caps AI spending next.
